The direct callers are all in `openmrs-module-webservices.rest`, under the generic `/ws/rest/v1` resources. There are three production call sites and one test class. The repo is `github.com/openmrs/openmrs-module-webservices.rest`; `openmrs-core` isn't a valid name for Falkon, so I used the full `github.com/openmrs/...` form.

**The changed declaration:** `OrderService.getOrderTypes(boolean includeRetired)` at `openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/OrderService.java:811`. It is implemented in `OrderServiceImpl.java:1002`, which delegates to `OrderDAO`. Falkon also returns a `getOrderTypes()` with no arguments on `OrderSearchCriteria`, which is a different method and is not analysed here.

**Confirmed affected REST code (strongest first):**

1. **`OrderTypeResource1_10.doGetAll`** (lines 120–123) returns `getOrderTypes(context.getIncludeAll())` wrapped in `NeedsPaging`. This backs `GET /ws/rest/v1/ordertype`. Any change to which types are returned, or to how retired types are filtered, changes the list output directly.
2. **`OrderTypeResource1_10.doSearch`** (lines 128–139) takes the same list and removes non-matching names with `iterator.remove()`. It therefore depends on the returned list being mutable. If the core change returned an unmodifiable or lazily-backed list, search would throw rather than just return different data.
3. **`OrderableResource1_10.search`** (lines 64–123) calls `getOrderTypes(false)` at line 69, then uses the result to collect concept classes and to match the `orderTypes` request parameter by UUID. This backs the `/ws/rest/v1/orderable` search. A change in which types are included, or in their `getConceptClasses()` contents, changes the concept search scope.
4. **`OrderableResource1_10.getOrderableConceptClasses`** (lines 134–148) consumes the list directly, calling `type.getConceptClasses()` on each element. A null element or a null concept-class collection would cause a failure here.
5. **`OrderTypeController1_10Test`** (test, not production) uses `getOrderTypes(false)` and `getOrderTypes(true)` for expected counts and assertions (lines 55, 99, 147, 157). These tests would need updating if the counts or inclusion rules change.

**Likely but not verified:**

- `OrderResource1_10` (line 257) looks up `OrderTypeResource1_10` via `RestService`. It does not call `getOrderTypes`, so it is only affected if the resource's single-item lookup depends on the same behaviour. I did not read that code.

**Not checked:**

- I did not read the surrounding code for the `OrderTypeResource1_10` test class or the `OrderableResource1_10` test class beyond what the grep showed. Neither calls `getOrderTypes` directly.
- The TypeScript consumers of `/ws/rest/v1/ordertype` and `/ws/rest/v1/orderable` in the ESM repositories (for example `openmrs-esm-patient-chart`, `openmrs-esm-patient-management`, `openmrs-esm-billing-app`) are outside the Java module. I did not search them. They would be affected only through the REST output, not through the Java call.
- Within `openmrs-core`, `OrderServiceImpl.java:1109` and `OrderTypeValidator.java:81` also call `getOrderTypes`. They are core callers, not part of the REST module, so they are excluded from the list below.
